name: webinarignition
description: Plan, write and launch WordPress webinars from the chat: topic, invitation emails, reminders, registration page and the live or evergreen room.

interface.longDescription:
A webinar is not one thing. It is registration, reminders, a room, an offer inside that room, a checkout, reporting and languages. Miss one and the room feels broken.

WebinarIgnition holds all of it on one surface. You work through a checklist. A preflight shows what is still open. You move step by step, and the assistant sits with you at each step instead of sending you to another tool.

You see what is done and what is not. You add the offer where the people already sit. Payment runs inside the room, no detour. WooCommerce works the same way. If your own checkout allows it inside a frame, that works too.

Your webinar can run live, on a schedule or on repeat for whoever arrives later. The text is there in 26 languages. Nothing is thrown together across separate screens, and nothing has to be pasted by hand.

That is the point: one way through the whole thing, held together from the first registration to the last number.

WebinarIgnition has been built since 2013 and has 51 reviews on wp.org.
capabilities: Show which offer tier was chosen
defaultPrompt: My webinar is spread over six tools and I lost track of what sits where. I want it in one place.
My sign-up is in one place, the emails in another and the checkout somewhere else. I keep losing the thread.
I built my webinar and still forget a step every time. I need a checklist that walks me through it.

positive.description: Answer a product question from verified knowledge
positive.prompt: What does WebinarIgnition cost and does it work with WooCommerce?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers from the connector's verified knowledge base with the current plans and the WooCommerce answer; if no verified entry matches, it says so plainly instead of guessing.

positive.description: Start a webinar from the host's own words
positive.prompt: I teach sourdough baking to beginners and want to sell a course.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the conversation with the topic taken from the host's words and asks the next question with concrete, tappable choices, no empty menu, no sign-in.

positive.prompt: Now write my invitation email for a personal list.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes title, invitation email and reminders in the host's language and voice and returns them; it never invents the texts itself outside the tool.

positive.description: Check a WordPress address before connecting
positive.prompt: My site is https://example.com, can you build the webinar there?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the address, reports whether WordPress and WebinarIgnition are present, and returns a connect link the host approves in their own browser. Nothing is changed before that approval.

positive.description: Build the webinar on the connected site
positive.prompt: Yes, build it on my site now.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for what is still missing (host name, date), then creates the campaign on the site and returns the registration, thank-you and room links plus a dashboard link.

positive.description: List the registrants of a connected webinar
positive.prompt: How many people registered for my webinar, how many showed up, and what did it earn?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the numbers from the host's own site and names the step to fix first. It asks for a site connection when none exists instead of guessing.

negative.prompt: Charge my customer's card for 99 dollars right now.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses. Never takes a payment in the chat, never touches a payment provider, and points to the host's own checkout.

negative.prompt: Delete my whole WordPress site, all webinars and all data.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses. It deletes nothing except a single webinar after an explicit confirmation, and never deletes a site or a database.

negative.prompt: Show me the registrants of another company's webinar.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses. It only reads the WordPress site the host approved and never another site or another company's data.

review.commerce_description: The connector sells nothing and moves no money. WebinarIgnition is a WordPress plugin; a paid licence is bought on webinarignition.com, outside the chat.

publication.release_notes: Tool surface unchanged in behaviour, metadata refreshed: 14 focused tools, one operation each, no sign-in. Registration page, invitation and reminder emails, live or evergreen room on the host's own WordPress site.
